hero.title: I help you work out, build and secure your app.
hero.text: Mobile apps and websites for businesses and startups – from the first idea to secure operation.

services.title: How I can help
services.intro: You can start anywhere – from a first idea to a review of a finished app. I don't leave security until the end; it is part of the work from the first design.

plan.title: Work it out
plan.text: I help you clarify whether a digital product makes sense, which one, and what you want from it.

secure.title: Secure

grow.title: Grow

points: Further versions driven by data and feedback
From MVP to a complete product

work.experiencesText: The projects my experience comes from – from smart buildings, agriculture and startups to banking and the public sector.

smart-buildings.title: Controlling homes and buildings
smart-buildings.text: A smart-technology supplier puts this iOS and Android app in the hands of homeowners and the managers of offices and buildings. It controls devices in real time through the buildings' control systems. I keep developing it – from the idea and UX through development and the backend to securing the communication.

agriculture.title: An operations app for smart stables
agriculture.text: An app for stable managers that a technology manufacturer supplies to its customers: sensors, ventilation, lighting and alerts. The interface is tailored to the people who work with it every day.

startup.title: An MVP in the App Store in two weeks
startup.text: An app a startup used to test a new product: users complete daily tasks with a coach and follow their progress. Data from the first users then fed discovery and business analysis, which set the product's next direction.

public-app.title: A map with reports from people
public-app.text: A map app in which people report the current state of places in the field and plan trips accordingly. Organisations manage their places in an admin, and the backend watches for outdated data on its own.

regulated.title: Apps in a regulated environment
regulated.text: For more than five years I developed native iOS apps for banks and the public sector – including biometric signing and secure document handling. I also contributed to the architecture of apps used by tens of thousands of people.

web-ai.title: Websites and AI-powered tools
web-ai.text: Company websites, landing pages and Python backends connected to language models – for example a tool that summarises entire YouTube playlists.

security.title: Security from the first line
security.text: Apps are built faster than ever, often with AI. Speed brings holes too: exposed data, leaked keys or AI features that can be abused. I review your app and fix what I find.

checks.title: Access to data
checks.text: Does every user see only what they should? I check permissions in the app, the API and the database.

checks.title: Keys and passwords
checks.text: I find access keys and passwords that leaked into the app, the code or the repository.

checks.title: Server and communication
checks.text: I review the server setup and how securely the app talks to the backend and to devices.

checks.title: AI features and agents
checks.text: I check that the AI in your app can't be abused and has no more permissions than it needs.

security.note: This is a practical review with fixes, not a certified penetration test.

approach.title: How I work
approach.intro: I don't have a fixed process – every business and every project is different. First I listen: what you do, what you need and what you have already tried. Then I tell you what I think and suggest the next step.

free.title: Free introductory consultation
free.text: 60–90 minutes, in person or online, about development or security. We go through your situation and you leave with a summary and a proposed next step – no obligation.

principles.title: Understand first, then build
principles.text: I ask about the goal, not just features. Sometimes the best advice is not to build yet.

principles.title: Security from the start
principles.text: I deal with security from the first design, not after launch, when every fix costs more.

principles.title: Clear agreements
principles.text: We agree scope, price and the next step in advance. After each part you can decide again.

about.title: One person. A team of AI agents.
bio: I'm Jakub Smolík. For more than six years I have been designing and developing apps – for banks, the public sector, large companies and startups. On the projects I lead, I am responsible as the technical lead for the whole solution: from design through the app and backend to securing servers and the communication with devices.

Technology is a tool for me, not the goal: what interests me is what the product will bring you. I don't join other companies' teams as one more developer by the hour – I take on products I can be responsible for as a whole. I'm based in Prague and happy to come to a meeting.

ai.title: How I work with AI agents
ai.workspaceAlt: Jakub Smolík at work at a desk with a monitor and a laptop
paragraphs: Research, drafts, coding, tests and documentation I do together with a team of AI agents. That lets me handle a scope that would otherwise need a small team – faster and without agency overhead. Decisions, review and responsibility for the result stay with me.
Your data stays protected: sensitive data and know-how I process only with local models on my own computer and never send to cloud AI tools. Hence smolikja team – me and my team of AI agents.

assurances.title: What you can count on

items.title: The product is yours
items.text: I hand over the code at agreed milestones, or it lives in your repository from the start. You own the App Store and Google Play accounts and the production servers – I'm happy to help set them up.

items.title: Someone else can pick it up
items.text: I use mainstream technologies and every project has detailed documentation. If our collaboration ends, I hand the project over properly.

items.title: Schedules with a buffer
items.text: I plan with room for the unexpected. I announce holidays in advance and we adjust the plan, so you always know where things stand.

assurances.note: We set out the details in the contract for your project.

items.question: How much does app development cost?
items.answer: It depends on what the app should do and which systems it connects to – a simple first version costs an order of magnitude less than a large system. After the introductory consultation I propose the approach and the price. For a clearly defined brief I offer a fixed price; for incremental development we agree a budget and priorities.

items.question: Do I need a finished brief?
items.answer: No. The introductory consultation is free and is there for me to understand your situation and goals. More detailed research, analysis or design I price according to the agreed scope, and I start only once you approve it.

items.question: How long does a first version take?
items.answer: It depends on the scope. A simple first version can be in the App Store within a few weeks, a larger product within a few months. I give an estimate once it's clear what the first version should do.

items.question: Can you review an app you didn't build?
items.answer: Yes. I review apps and websites from other suppliers, from in-house teams and those built with AI tools, and help fix what I find. We agree the scope of the review in advance.

items.question: Why one person and not an agency?
items.answer: You talk directly to the person who designs, builds and secures the product – nothing gets lost in handoffs, and one person is accountable for the result. AI agents give me the capacity of a small team. If your project needed many people working in parallel from day one, I'll tell you.

items.question: What if you're not available?
items.answer: I plan schedules with a buffer so there is room for the unexpected, and I always let you know where things stand. I announce holidays in advance. You hold the code, documentation and accounts, so another developer can pick up the project at any time. We write the specific rules into the contract.

items.question: How do you use AI, and what happens to my data?
items.answer: AI agents help me with research, drafts, code, tests and documentation; I make the decisions and review the work. Sensitive data and know-how I process only with local models on my own computer – I don't send them to cloud AI tools. We agree at the start what you consider sensitive, and if you like, we sign a non-disclosure agreement.

items.question: Can you take over an existing app?
items.answer: Yes. First I assess the existing app – including its security – and propose the best next step. A rewrite from scratch is not the default recommendation.

securityPage.metaDescription: I review the security of your mobile app, website or backend – including ones built with AI – and fix what I find. Free introductory consultation.
securityPage.title: Reviewing and securing apps
securityPage.intro: Apps are built faster than ever – in-house, by different suppliers or with AI. I check whether yours is secure, explain clearly what I found and fix the problems.

evidence.text: According to Veracode's 2026 research, on average only 56% of AI-written code passed a security test.
evidence.linkLabel: Source: SD Times on the Veracode report

audience.title: Who I help
items: Businesses and startups before launching an app or website
People who built their app themselves or with AI tools
Companies adding AI features and agents to their products
Suppliers whose customers ask them to demonstrate security – for example because of NIS2 or the CRA

items.title: App and backend review
items.text: I go through the code of your mobile app, website and server and their setup: sign-in and credential storage, permissions, APIs, logs, databases and cloud services. You get a clear report and fixes in the code.

items.title: Apps built with AI
items.text: I review apps from tools such as Lovable, Bolt or Cursor: data access rules, exposed keys and unprotected APIs – the most common weaknesses of quickly built apps.

items.title: Secure AI features and agents
items.text: I design or review the AI features in your app: model keys on the server, cost limits, agent permissions and resistance to abuse through prompt injection.

items.title: Secure development and release
items.text: I set up automatic checks that watch every change for leaked keys and vulnerable libraries, and prepare a list of the components you use (SBOM).

items.title: Communication with servers and devices
items.text: I secure the connection between the app, the server and devices – including smart buildings and their control systems.

items.title: Material for customers and regulation
items.text: I prepare the technical part of supplier security questionnaires and of preparing for NIS2 or the CRA. Legal interpretation I leave to lawyers.

steps.title: We agree the scope
steps.text: In the free introductory consultation we discuss what to review and how. We confirm the scope and permission to test in writing.

steps.title: Analysis
steps.text: I go through the code and setup with specialised tools and with AI – with your consent, and sensitive parts only locally on my own computer.

steps.title: Manual verification
steps.text: I verify and document every finding myself. Nothing goes into the report that I haven't confirmed.

steps.title: A clear report
steps.text: You get the findings ordered by severity, explained without unnecessary jargon.

steps.title: Fixes
steps.text: If you like, I fix the problems straight away – finished code changes, not just a list of issues.

items.title: I build apps myself
items.text: I know where their weak spots tend to be and can fix them directly.

items.title: Experience in a regulated environment
items.text: For more than five years I developed apps for banks and the public sector – including biometric signing and secure document handling.

items.title: Security in practice
items.text: On the projects I lead, I secure servers and the communication of apps with the backend and with devices in smart buildings.

items.title: Your data stays with me
items.text: I process sensitive code and data only with local models and never send them to cloud AI tools.

limits.title: What I don't do
limits.text: This is not a certified penetration test, nor a formal audit under cybersecurity law or ISO. If you need one, I'll tell you straight away and advise you how to proceed.

items.question: Is this a penetration test?
items.answer: Not in the certified sense. It is a practical review of the code, setup and behaviour of the app with verified findings and fixes. If you need a certified penetration test, for example for a tender, I'll tell you straight away.

items.question: Do you need access to the source code?
items.answer: Ideally yes – reviewing the code reveals the most. Some checks are possible without it. We agree the access and what I may test in advance and confirm it in writing.

items.question: Will you send my code to an AI?
items.answer: Only with your consent. Sensitive parts I process with local models on my own computer, so they never leave it.

items.question: How much does a review cost?
items.answer: It depends on the size of the app and the scope of the review. After the free introductory consultation I give you a fixed price.

items.question: What if you find a serious problem?
items.answer: I let you know immediately, not in the final report, and propose the quickest safe fix.

privacy.metaDescription: What data smolikja.team processes, why and for how long.
privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: This page describes which personal data I process on smolikja.team, for what purpose and what rights you have.

sections.title: Who processes the data
paragraphs: The data controller is {operator}. For anything concerning personal data, contact me at {email}.

sections.title: Contact form
paragraphs: When you write to me through the form, I process your name, e-mail address and the text of your message. The purpose is to answer your enquiry and arrange a possible collaboration; the legal basis is pre-contractual negotiation and my legitimate interest in handling the enquiry.

The message is delivered to my mailbox by Resend (Resend, Inc., USA) acting as a processor. I keep the data for as long as needed to handle the enquiry and any resulting collaboration, then delete it.
To protect the form from abuse I briefly keep a hash of the sender's IP address; it expires after 24 hours at most.

sections.title: Cookies and analytics
paragraphs: The site uses no analytics or marketing cookies and does not track your behaviour. It stores a single technical cookie, NEXT_LOCALE, with the language you chose, valid for one year.

sections.title: Your rights
paragraphs: You have the right to access your data, to have it corrected or erased, to restrict processing and to object. Just write to the e-mail above. You can also lodge a complaint with the Czech Office for Personal Data Protection.
